candidate_axiom.name: Functorial State Evolution & Morphism Preservation
candidate_axiom.statement: Every architectural state transformation must operate as a structure-preserving functor across subsystem categories, guaranteeing that component composition in the problem domain is preserved under compilation into execution morphisms.
candidate_axiom.operational_rule: State transitions that violate functorial morphism preservation across subcomponents are rejected at compile time.

system_profile.topology_diagram:
[Category C: Domain Objects] ──> [Functor F] ──> [Category D: Compiled Morphisms]
               │                                                    │
      Composition f o g                                   Preserved F(f) o F(g)
               │                                                    │
               ▼                                                    ▼
      [Domain Verification]                               [Execution Engine Runtime]

Functorial Mapping Layer.role: Maps subsystem composition in problem space directly to execution morphisms.
Functorial Mapping Layer.invariant_rule: F(f o g) = F(f) o F(g) must be verified at compile time.

Identity Morphism Guard.role: Guarantees that null operations preserve identity across subsystem interfaces.
Identity Morphism Guard.invariant_rule: F(id_A) = id_F(A) must hold without side-effects.

Category Type Verifier.role: Guarantees associative morphism composition across component categories.

tradeoffs.constraints: All component interfaces must be formalized as category objects and morphisms.
